q: On which planet is Tress of the Emerald Sea set?
explain: Lumar is a world of spore oceans fed by twelve moons, each hosting an aether.

q: What does Tress love to collect at the start of her story?
explain: Tress treasures her cups for the stories each one seems to tell.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea, ch. 1

q: What kind of animal is Huck, Tress's talking companion?
explain: Huck is a cursed talking rat who secretly spies for the Sorceress.

q: Who is Charlie, the young man Tress sets out to rescue?
explain: The duke sent Charlie to the Midnight Sea, where he was captured by the Sorceress.

q: Who captains the pirate ship Crow's Song when Tress joins its crew?
explain: Captain Crow is a ruthless pirate whom Tress eventually outwits.

q: What happens when verdant spores come into contact with water?
explain: Sailors use verdant vines as fuses or to entangle opponents.

q: Which spores release a burst of air when wet, making them ideal for firing cannons?
explain: Zephyr spores fall on the Sapphire Sea and are used to propel cannonballs.

q: What is Fort's position aboard the Crow's Song?
explain: Fort is deaf and communicates through a Nalthian board.

q: What does Dr. Ulaam, the Crow's Song's surgeon, ask for as payment?
explain: Hoid claims Ulaam is the best doctor he has ever met, despite his odd fee.

q: Who does the crew elect as captain after Crow is removed?
explain: Tress trades Crow to the dragon Xisis, and the grateful crew chooses her to lead.

q: What is the name of the new ship Tress and her crew buy at the end of the story?
explain: Pardoned by the king, the crew sell the Crow's Song and buy the Two Cups, with Charlie aboard as valet, storyteller and musician.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Two Cups

q: In which of Lumar's seas does the dragon Xisis make his home?
explain: Xisis is a dragon originally from Yolen who, for a time, made his home in the Crimson Sea.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Xisis

q: On which planet do Yumi and Painter live?
explain: Komashi is the world where the Shard Virtuosity Splintered herself.

q: What does Yumi stack into delicate towers to summon spirits?
explain: The spirits she draws grant blessings to the villagers of her land.

q: What does Painter hunt and capture with his brush and ink?
explain: Nightmares seep out of the shroud, and painters trap them by painting them into harmless images.

q: What sacred title does Yumi hold among her people?
explain: A yoki-hijo summons spirits for her people at great cost to her own freedom.

q: What is Painter's real name?
explain: Nikaro usually goes by Painter, after his job as a nightmare painter.

q: What hangs permanently over the city of Kilahito?
explain: Under the shroud Kilahito lives in constant darkness, lit by glowing hion lines.

q: In which two colors do Kilahito's hion lines glow?
explain: Hion lines run through the city, providing both light and power.

q: Who is Yumi's strict guardian and attendant?
explain: Liyun oversees Yumi's rigid daily rituals as a yoki-hijo.

q: Which of these characters is a fellow nightmare painter in Kilahito?
explain: Painter meets Akane and Tojin on patrol at the city's western edge.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter, ch. 1

q: What is Masaka, who works as a nightmare painter, secretly?
explain: Masaka hides her true nature and later helps Yumi and Design map the lands beyond the shroud.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter; Coppermind: Masaka

q: Which Shard Splintered herself on Komashi?
explain: The remnants of Virtuosity's power shaped the strange Investiture of Komashi.

q: On which planet is The Sunlit Man set?
explain: Canticle is a world scorched by a deadly, Invested sun.

q: Why must the cities of Canticle keep constantly moving?
explain: Anyone caught in Canticle's direct sunlight is burned to ash.

q: Who is the woman Nomad befriends and helps on Canticle?
explain: Rain becomes Nomad's key ally in standing against the Cinder King.

q: By what name was Nomad known when he lived on Roshar?
explain: Sigzil was a member of Bridge Four before becoming the worldhopping Nomad.

q: Which group hunts Nomad from world to world?
explain: Nomad keeps Skipping between planets to stay ahead of the Night Brigade.

q: Which tyrant do Nomad and Rain oppose on Canticle?
explain: The Cinder King commands the Charred, people enslaved by a corrupted sunheart driven into their chests.

q: What does Nomad's Torment make him unable to do?
explain: The Torment stops him from causing harm even in self-defense.

q: What is the cause of Nomad's Torment?
explain: Holding a Dawnshard leaves a lasting mark on whoever carried it.

q: What kind of being is Auxiliary, Nomad's talking companion?
explain: Aux was nearly destroyed by the Dawnshard Nomad once held and survives as a voice in Nomad's head.

q: On which planet is White Sand set?
explain: Taldain is tidally locked, split into an eternal Dayside and Darkside.

q: What do Sand Masters expend from their own bodies to control sand?
explain: Overusing sand mastery can dangerously dehydrate a Sand Master.

q: Who is Kenton's father, the powerful Lord Mastrell?
explain: Praxton dies fighting the Kerztians, his final attack burying Kenton in sand.

q: What color does white sand turn after a Sand Master uses it?
explain: Spent sand turns white again after about four hours in Dayside's sunlight.

q: What is distinctive about Taldain's Darkside?
a: It always faces a dim star
explain: Khriss hails from Darkside, which faces a white dwarf hidden behind a particle ring.

q: What is the name of the order of Sand Masters that Kenton belongs to?
explain: Kenton eventually becomes Lord Mastrell, leader of the Diem.

q: Which Shard Invests Taldain through its blazing larger star?
explain: Taldain orbits a blue-white supergiant paired with a dim white dwarf.
source: Arcanum Unbounded, Taldain system essay; Coppermind: Taldain system

q: On which planet is Sixth of the Dusk set?
explain: First of the Sun is an ocean world dotted with deadly islands.

q: What are the talent-granting birds of First of the Sun called?
explain: Young Aviar must visit the island of Patji to gain their talents.

q: What is Dusk's profession?
explain: Dusk traps Aviar on Patji, as was the tradition among his people.

q: Patji, the largest island of the Pantheon, is often called what?
explain: Trappers like Dusk treat the deadly island of Patji with wary reverence, as a stern father.

q: What does Dusk's Aviar Sak show him?
explain: Sak's corpse visions warn Dusk of danger ahead; her talent was unknown among Aviar before her.

q: What talent does Dusk's Aviar Kokerlii grant him?
explain: On Patji, many predators hunt by sensing minds, so Kokerlii is vital.

q: On which planet do the Forests of Hell grow?
explain: The Forests of Hell are haunted by shades, the spirits of the dead.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: What does Silence Montane run in the Forests of Hell?
explain: Silence runs the waystop with her daughter, William Ann.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: Which metal can destroy the shades of Threnody?
explain: Shades grow enraged if someone lights a fire, runs at night or sheds blood.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: Under what secret identity does Silence hunt bounties?
explain: Silence uses the bounties she collects to keep her waystop out of debt.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: What became of Silence's grandmother after she was killed?
a: Her shade is bound in a shrine
wrong: She was buried in the Homeland
explain: Silence's grandmother came from the Homeland before it fell to the Evil.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell; Coppermind: Silence's grandmother
